subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a separate assistant action-token search path, and what token containment, read-target policy, and scope rules should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but workspace-wide search using event-scoped Slack credentials is a security and product boundary that automation should not define without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
options.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` in the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, read-target/privacy enforcement, docs, focused tests, and redacted live Slack proof.

options.title: Consolidate Slack search first
options.body: Define one Slack search contract that covers RTS and user-token `search.messages` before accepting implementation work.

options.title: Defer workspace search
options.body: Keep this issue open but block implementation until maintainers are ready to own the token and privacy model.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
recommendation.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` in the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, read-target/privacy enforcement, docs, focused tests, and redacted live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame routes the affected Slack assistant/action surfaces to this contributor, and the decision is about those Slack plugin boundaries.
